n103.point: Respondents are Hisense USA Corporation, Hisense Co., Ltd., Hisense International Co., Ltd., and Hisense Visual Technology Co. Ltd., collectively referred to as "Hisense."
n103.quote: Respondents Hisense USA Corporation, Hisense Co., Ltd., Hisense International Co., Ltd., and Hisense Visual Technology Co. Ltd. (collectively "Hisense") hereby answers the Complaint

n104.point: Hisense denies all allegations that it has engaged in unfair competition or infringement, denies that it has imported, sold for importation, or sold infringing products, denies that a domestic industry exists as required by Section 337, and denies that complainants are entitled to any relief.
n104.quote: Hisense denies that it has engaged in acts of unfair competition in violation of Section 337 by importing, selling for importation, and/or selling after importation into the United States any product that infringes the asserted patents.

n105.point: The asserted patents are U.S. Patent No. 7,705,948 (the '948 patent), independent claim 1, and U.S. Patent No. 7,570,334 (the '334 patent), independent claim 1.
n105.quote: Hisense admits that Complainants assert independent claim 1 of U.S. Patent No. 7,705,948 (the '948 patent') and independent claim 1 of U.S. Patent No. 7,570,334

n106.point: Hisense's "Accused Products" are televisions containing liquid crystal display (LCD) panels manufactured by HKC Corporation Ltd., as defined by the instituted scope of the investigation.
n106.quote: Hisense understands Hisense's ""Accused Products" to mean televisions that contain liquid crystal display (LCD") panels manufactured by HKC Corporation Ltd., that are accused of infringing

n107.point: Hisense asserts that it does not literally infringe any valid and enforceable claim of the asserted patents because at least one claim element is not met for each asserted claim.
n107.quote: On information and belief, Hisense does not literally infringe any valid and enforceable claim of the asserted patents. On information and belief, at least one claim element is not met

n108.point: Hisense argues that complainants are barred from relying on the doctrine of equivalents to allege infringement because of the all-elements rule, vitiation, intentional narrow claiming, prosecution history estoppel, prior art estoppel, and the disclosure-dedication doctrine.
n108.quote: Complainants are barred from relying on the doctrine of equivalents to allege infringement of any valid and enforceable claim of the asserted patents because of the all-elements rule, vitiation, intentional narrow claiming, prosecution history estoppel, prior art estoppel

n109.point: Hisense argues that any claims of indirect infringement are barred because Hisense did not know the internal structure of HKC LCD panels, did not commit affirmative acts to encourage infringement, and did not know that induced acts were infringing.
n109.quote: any claims of indirect infringement are barred at least because Hisense did not and does not "know" what the internal structure, arrangement, and geometry are of the elements of the LCD panels

n11.point: The '948 patent relates to LCD devices with a substrate containing an upper electrode layer with slits, an insulating layer, and a lower electrode layer, where the slit geometry reduces disclination and improves light transmission, image quality, and manufacturing yield.
n11.quote: the '948 patent claims inventions that relate to LCD devices comprising a substrate with an upper electrode layer having slits formed on it, an insulating layer between the substrate and the upper electrode layer, and a lower electrode layer

n110.quote: the Hisense TV model 32A4H cannot be an infringing product when it does not contain an HKC LCD panel and instead contains an LCD panel provided by Complainants' licensee

n111.quote: the only HKC product identified in Complainants' claim chart for the '334 patent has been discontinued according to the website relied on by Complainants in this Complaint, and this specific HKC product has not been used in the Hisense TV model 32A4H

n112.point: Complainants have not identified which, if any, specific HKC product is contained in any Hisense TV product.
n112.quote: In this paragraph, Complainants fail to identify which, if any, specific HKC product is contained in any Hisense TV product.

n113.point: Hisense denies that Complainants have adequately alleged and cannot prove the existence of a domestic industry as required by Section 337(a)(2) and (a)(3).
n113.quote: Complainants have not adequately alleged and cannot prove the existence of a domestic industry, as required by Section 337(a)(2) and defined by Section 337(a)(3)

n114.point: Hisense asserts that Complainants cannot establish that any products of licensee Innolux Corporation practice at least one valid and enforceable claim of the asserted patents.
n114.quote: Complainants cannot establish that any products of licensee Innolux Corporation practice at least one valid and enforceable claim of the asserted patents

n115.quote: The Asserted Claims are invalid for failing to comply with one or more of the conditions for patentability set forth in Part II of Title 35 of the United States Code, including but not limited to 35 U.S.C. §§ 102, 103, 112, and 256

n116.quote: Complainants are barred from enforcing any asserted claim of any of the Asserted Patents or from obtaining the requested relief by one or more of the doctrines of waiver, equitable estoppel, and acquiescence

n117.point: Hisense argues that Complainants have not adequately alleged and cannot establish that the requested relief is in the public interest, considering effects on public health, welfare, competitive conditions, domestic production of like articles, and consumers.
n117.quote: Complainants have not adequately alleged and cannot establish that the requested relief is in the public interest, after considering the effect of exclusion upon the public health and welfare, competitive conditions

n118.quote: To the extent any issue of claim construction, infringement, validity, or enforceability of the claims of the '948 patent in this Investigation is identical to issues that are litigated and adjudicated against one or more of the Complainants in Civil Action No. 2:23-CV-00515

n12.quote: the '334 patent claims inventions that relate to LCD panels comprising a pair of opposing substrates with a pixel region between them that contains a plurality of pixel electrodes arrayed on one of the two substrates

n120.quote: To the extent that Complainants' allegations of infringement relate to Hisense products that contain LCD panels provided by or for any named licensee of the Asserted Patents, or that contain LCD panels provided by or for a licensee of the Asserted Patents under a covenant not to sue, whether explicitly or impliedly, Complainants' claims are barred because Hisense has an express or implied license

n121.quote: To the extent that Hisense or its customers or suppliers import any accused products for, or sell any accused products to, the United States government, such acts are not subject to the requests for relief of Complainants

n130.point: Respondents contend that the inventor failed to disclose material prior art references including U.S. Patent App. Pub. No. 2005/0078240 (later U.S. Patent No. 7,196,353), U.S. Patent No. 6,433,841, U.S. Patent No. 6,611,301, and U.S. Patent No. 6,897,932, all listing Masao Murade as a named inventor and disclosing the 'dummy pixel' subject matter of claim 14.
n130.quote: Those withheld, material prior art references include at least the following references: U.S. Patent App. Pub. No. 2005/0078240 (later issued as U.S. Patent No. 7,196,353); U.S. Patent No. 6,433,841; U.S. Patent No. 6,611,301; and U.S. Patent No. 6,897,932.

n131.point: Respondents allege that the Examiner's allowance of claim 14 was based on the incorrect belief that prior art did not disclose the 'dummy pixel' limitation, and that the inventor knew this characterization was incorrect based on his own prior art references.
n131.quote: the Examiner stated that claim 14 of the '334 patent was patentable based on the incorrect belief that the prior art did not disclose or suggest the recited "dummy pixel" limitation of claim 14.

n132.point: Respondents allege the inventor deliberately withheld these material prior art references because he understood they would have led the Examiner to reject claim 14 as obvious.
n132.quote: Upon information and belief, and subject to further discovery, the inventor understood that his own "dummy pixel" prior art would have led the Examiner to reject claim 14 of the '334 patent, and therefore deliberately decided to withhold those references from the Examiner.

n133.point: Respondents argue that claim 14 was obtained through prosecution history where the Examiner rejected the original independent claim but allowed a dependent claim based on the belief that prior art did not render obvious the dummy pixel subject matter.
n133.quote: the Examiner stated that dependent claim 10 was allowable because the prior art—"alone or in combination"—did not "disclose or render obvious" the subject matter recited in dependent claim 10

n134.point: Respondents contend that the named inventor Masao Murade was aware of substantively identical dummy pixel subject matter in his own issued patents yet failed to disclose these references in any information disclosure statement during prosecution.
n134.quote: Despite this knowledge and awareness of substantively identical subject matter relating to dummy pixel electrodes claimed and described in his own issued patents, at no point during prosecution of the '334 patent did the named inventor disclose this prior art to the Examiner

n135.quote: the Examiner-cited Karasawa reference is the only English-language, U.S. Patent document cited on the face page of the '334 patent, with the remaining cited references all being Japanese-language Foreign Patent Documents.

about.text: The complainant, BH Innovations LLC (BHI), together with patent owners Longitude Licensing Limited and 138 East LCD Advancements Ltd., brought this investigation before the U.S. International Trade Commission under Section 337, a statute letting the Commission block imports that infringe U.S. patents. BHI is the exclusive licensee of two patents: U.S. Patent No. 7,705,948 ('the 948 patent'), covering LCD devices with a slitted electrode layer design said to reduce visual defects and improve manufacturing yield, and U.S. Patent No. 7,570,334 ('the 334 patent'), covering LCD panel designs with particular electrode and sealing structures. The accused technology is found in LCD devices generally: a liquid crystal layer sandwiched between glass substrates, with circuitry controlling light transmission through pixels to form images on screens such as televisions and computer monitors.

The named respondents were TCL entities (TCL Technology Group Corp., TTE Technology Inc., TCL Moka International, TCL Overseas Marketing, TCL King Electrical Appliances, TCL Industries Holdings, TCL Electronics Holdings, Shenzhen TCL New Technology, and TCL Smart Device (Vietnam)), LG Electronics Inc. and LG Electronics USA Inc., Hisense USA Corporation and related Hisense entities, HKC Corporation Ltd. and related HKC entities, and VIZIO Holding Corp. -- all alleged to manufacture, import, or sell televisions or monitors containing LCD panels, many supplied by HKC. The Commission instituted the investigation on November 24, 2025, covering alleged infringement of claim 1 of the 948 patent and claim 1 of the 334 patent by LCD devices, their components, and products containing them.

allegations.text: BHI alleged that each group of respondents violated Section 337 by importing into the United States, or selling for importation or after importation, LCD devices that infringe claim 1 of the 948 patent, the 334 patent, or both. Specifically, BHI alleged VIZIO's D32fM-K07 televisions (using HKC PT320CT01 panels) and TCL's 32S331 and 32S355 televisions (using HKC PT320AT02 panels) infringe the 334 patent; LG's 27MP40W monitors (using HKC NS270CS01 panels) infringe the 948 patent; and Hisense televisions and HKC's own panels and devices infringe claim 1 of both patents. BHI supported these importation allegations with receipts, delivery records, and photographs showing manufacture in China (for TCL, LG, VIZIO, and HKC products) or Mexico (for Hisense products) and subsequent importation into the United States.

BHI alleged that the domestic industry requirement -- the requirement that a complainant show a qualifying U.S. economic activity tied to the patent -- was satisfied through Innolux Corporation and its U.S. subsidiaries, which BHI said manufacture and sell licensed LCD panels practicing the 948 and 334 patents (found in products such as tablets), and which engage in substantial U.S. research, development, engineering, testing, repair, and customer support activities, along with significant revenues and spare-parts inventories tied to the patents.

BHI requested that the Commission issue a permanent limited exclusion order (an order barring the specified infringing imports from entering the United States) against the named respondents' infringing LCD devices, permanent cease and desist orders (orders barring further U.S. sale, marketing, or use of infringing inventory) against the respondents, and the imposition of a bond during the 60-day Presidential review period that follows any Commission exclusion order.

paragraphs.text: The TCL respondents denied infringing any valid claim of the asserted patents and denied that a domestic industry exists, arguing complainants had not shown Innolux's U.S. investments met the statutory thresholds. They asserted the asserted claims are invalid under 35 U.S.C. §§ 101, 102, 103, 112, 116, and/or 256 over prior art, and raised numerous other defenses including prosecution history estoppel, patent exhaustion/license, inventorship, ensnarement, prosecution laches, and public-interest objections to any exclusion order.

summary.headline: BH Innovations LLC and related patent owners accused TCL, LG Electronics, Hisense, HKC, and VIZIO of importing and selling televisions and monitors using infringing liquid crystal display (LCD) panels, but the Commission terminated the investigation after complainants withdrew the complaint.

standing.text: The investigation was terminated in its entirety as to all respondents. The Administrative Law Judge granted complainants' second amended unopposed motion to terminate the investigation based on withdrawal of the complaint, and denied other pending motions in the same order. The Commission subsequently determined not to review that initial determination, letting it stand and formally terminating the investigation. No infringement, validity, domestic industry, or remedy determination was reached, and no exclusion order or cease and desist order is in force.
